Operator: Good day, and welcome to the SecureNet Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by the pound sign. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Casey Wong, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Casey Wong: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SecureNet Technologies' results for the Q3 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer, and Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Casey, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. SecureNet Technologies had an exceptional Q3, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. We are seeing significant traction with our cloud-native security platform and are benefiting from the increased focus on cybersecurity across all industries. The impact of our new AI-powered threat detection, SecureXDR 5.0, is evident in the reduced incident response times reported by our customers.

Before diving into the numbers, I'd like to provide some color on the evolving threat landscape, as it's the North Star guiding our product roadmap, R&D investments, and go-to-market strategy. Cybersecurity isn't static—it's a high-velocity arms race where adversaries leverage cutting-edge tech like generative AI, quantum computing threats, and weaponized supply chains to outpace defenders. Our team at SecureNet is not just reacting; we're anticipating and architecting resilience at scale.

According to the latest Mandiant M-Trends report, which aligns closely with our own telemetry from protecting over 4,500 enterprise customers, median dwell time for attackers in environments has dropped to just 10 days—a 30% reduction year-over-year—thanks to improved EDR and XDR detection. But the volume of threats has exploded: we observed a 62% year-over-year increase in high-severity incidents across our global SOC, with ransomware remaining the kingpin at 28% of engagements, up from 19% last year. Payout demands have surged, averaging $1.8 million per incident per IBM's Cost of a Data Breach study, and we've seen a 250% spike in AI-generated phishing campaigns mimicking legitimate tools like Microsoft Teams or Slack—often evading legacy signature-based defenses by 85% on first pass.

Diving deeper into ransomware, LockBit and BlackCat variants dominated Q3, exploiting unpatched vulnerabilities in Ivanti VPNs and Citrix gateways, much like the MOVEit Transfer breach earlier this year that impacted millions. Our SecureXDR platform blocked over 1.2 million such attempts in Q3 alone, a 45% increase from Q2, underscoring the efficacy of our behavioral AI models trained on the MITRE ATT&CK framework. Supply chain attacks are another red-hot vector—think SolarWinds 2.0—with a 180% year-over-year rise in third-party compromise attempts, per our data. We've instrumented zero-trust segmentation in 70% of our Fortune 1000 deployments to mitigate lateral movement, reducing blast radius by an average of 92%.

Regionally, the landscape is fracturing. In the Americas, which drove 52% of our Q3 bookings, we're seeing a surge in nation-state espionage tied to critical infrastructure—OT/ICS attacks up 75% year-over-year, fueled by tensions around elections and energy grids. Customers like a major U.S. utility are layering our OT-specific modules atop our SASE for air-gapped segmentation. EMEA, at 28% of revenue, is compliance-heavy: NIS2 and DORA mandates have accelerated zero-trust adoption, with our EU customer base growing 40% quarter-over-quarter. We've seen a 110% uptick in ransomware targeting healthcare under GDPR pressures—our Sovereign Cloud offerings, compliant with Schrems II, helped a Big Four bank thwart a €50 million demand last month. APAC, our fastest-growing region at 22% of ARR growth, faces sophisticated APTs from Lazarus Group affiliates; we've partnered with regional telcos like Singtel to deploy deception tech, luring attackers into honeypots and cutting mean time to respond to under 2 hours.

Strategically, we're leaning into three pillars to stay ahead. First, AI-native defense: Our GenAI Shield uses multimodal LLMs to detect deepfake voice phishing and polymorphic malware, achieving 98.7% true positive rates in red-team simulations—outpacing competitors by 15% in independent AV-TEST benchmarks. We've allocated $250 million to R&D this year, with 40% focused on post-quantum cryptography to counter Harvest Now, Decrypt Later threats from nation-states. Second, platform convergence: SecureXDR plus SASE in a single pane—our Nexus One unified console reduced alert fatigue by 65% for early adopters, driving 35% upsell in existing accounts. Third, ecosystem orchestration: Integrations with Okta for identity threat detection and Zscaler's ZPA have expanded our total addressable market into SSE, where we're targeting 25% share in cloud-native workloads.

These dynamics directly fuel our financials: threat-informed selling contributed to 28% year-over-year revenue growth to $285 million in Q3, with 92% gross margins intact. Customer retention hit 98%, and net expansion reached 128%, as breaches like Change Healthcare remind boards that downtime costs $10 million per day. Looking forward, we expect the threat landscape to intensify—ransomware-as-a-service marketplaces maturing, quantum risks materializing by 2026 per NIST timelines—but SecureNet is positioned as the indispensable platform.

Our overall strategy is centered around five core pillars: providing commentary on the evolving threat landscape as I just outlined, accelerating the number of new customers acquired, increasing average deal sizes for new and existing customers, managing the impact of currency fluctuations on revenue, and committing to a strong full-year revenue and profitability outlook.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we had a remarkable Q3. Revenue reached $785 million, reflecting a 28% year-over-year increase. This growth was fueled by both new customer acquisition and expansion within our existing customer base. Our gross margin remained strong at 82%, demonstrating our ability to scale efficiently. Operating expenses were $450 million, and net income was $180 million, translating to $1.05 per share. We are increasing our guidance for the full year based on these outstanding results.

I'm thrilled to dive deep into one of our strongest performance metrics this quarter: new customer acquisition. We onboarded 520 new customers in Q3, marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase from the 406 added in Q3 FY2023, and a solid 12% sequential growth from the 464 in Q2. This brings our total customer base to over 8,200 active accounts, up 22% year-over-year.

To give you the full picture, let's break this down by segment, region, and the strategic drivers. First, by customer tier: Enterprise large-scale deployments with ACV over $500K saw us add 185 new logos, up 35% year-over-year. This segment now represents 36% of our new wins, fueled by our Zero Trust Architecture suite, which integrates seamlessly with multi-cloud environments like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Key wins included a top-5 global bank adopting our full-stack XDR platform—combining EDR, NDR, and cloud workload protection—for their hybrid perimeter defense.

Mid-market and commercial with ACV $100K to $500K added 245 new customers, a standout 42% year-over-year surge, accounting for 47% of additions. Here, our SASE offering, SecureEdge, resonated strongly amid the shift to remote-hybrid workforces. We've seen SMBs and mid-market firms accelerating adoption post-ransomware waves, with integrations to popular IAM tools like Okta and Ping Identity driving stickiness.

Public sector and government added 90 new accounts, up 15% year-over-year, or 17% of total. Wins here were bolstered by FedRAMP Moderate authorization for our Sentinel AI threat hunting platform, positioning us competitively against incumbents like Palo Alto Networks' Prisma and CrowdStrike's Falcon platform.

Regionally, our expansion remains balanced but accelerating outside North America: North America had 286 new customers, up 22% year-over-year, representing 55%; EMEA 130, up 38%, 25%; APAC 104, up 42%, 20%. North America continues to anchor our growth, driven by CISA's heightened ransomware alerts and NIST 800-53 compliance mandates, with notable traction among financial services and healthcare verticals facing SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules.

EMEA's momentum reflects GDPR enforcement and NIS2 Directive tailwinds, where we secured 15 new DACH-region enterprises leveraging our data sovereignty-compliant cloud security posture management tools. APAC was our fastest grower, up 42% year-over-year, propelled by digital transformation in Southeast Asia and Australia's CDR regulations. Partnerships with telcos like Singtel and NTT have unlocked hyperscaler-adjacent deals, including 20 new customers via our AWS Marketplace listing for managed detection and response.

What's powering this? Product innovation like the launch of Sentinel AI in June generated 210 of our new customers—40% of the quarter's total. This GenAI-native platform uses behavioral anomaly detection with 98% accuracy in identifying zero-day exploits, outperforming legacy SIEMs like Splunk or Elastic in TCO benchmarks from Gartner's latest Magic Quadrant for SIEM. Ecosystem partnerships with 50+ ISV partners, including Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange and Microsoft Sentinel co-sell motions, contributed to 35% of pipeline conversion. Channel-led deals via hyperscalers hit a record 150 new customers. Market tailwinds like global cyber threats unrelenting—Verizon’s 2024 DBIR reported a 30% year-over-year rise in breaches involving vulnerabilities like Log4Shell derivatives—pushing CISOs toward consolidated platforms. Our net promoter score of 72 reflects this urgency, with 85% of new logos citing consolidation from point solutions as the trigger.

Strategically, we're doubling down on high-velocity segments. Our sales pipeline grew 40% quarter-over-quarter to $1.2 billion, with enterprise deal sizes averaging 18% larger year-over-year at $420K ACV. We maintained a pristine 98% gross retention rate, and expansion within new cohorts already at 15% in Q3—well ahead of industry averages per KeyBanc’s cybersecurity surveys. Looking forward, we guide to 550-600 new customers in Q4, supported by Q1 FY2025 launches like our sovereign cloud module for APAC data localization and deeper GenAI red-teaming capabilities. This positions SecureNet to capture share in a $200 billion-plus TAM, growing at 15% CAGR per IDC.

Next, I'd like to dive deep into average deal size, segmented by new and existing customers. This metric is a strong barometer of our land-and-expand strategy in the cybersecurity market, where enterprises are increasingly consolidating their security stacks around integrated platforms to combat sophisticated threats like ransomware-as-a-service and nation-state APTs.

In Q3, our average initial ACV for new customers came in at $450,000, representing a robust 25% year-over-year increase from $360,000 in Q3 FY2023. This acceleration was driven by a shift toward larger enterprise logos, with 68% of new deals exceeding $250,000 ACV, up from 52% last year. We're seeing this in deals with Fortune 500 financial services firms and healthcare providers, who are deploying our next-gen XDR platform—powered by our proprietary AI-driven behavioral analytics engine—with deeper integration into hybrid cloud environments via AWS Outposts and Azure Arc.

For existing customers, the average expansion deal size was even stronger at $750,000 in TCV, translating to an incremental ACV of approximately $320,000. This marked a 35% year-over-year uplift from last year. Our net revenue retention rate held steady at 128%, reflecting successful upsells into adjacent modules like our Zero Trust Network Access solution and Cloud Workload Protection Platform, which address the surging demand for SASE architectures amid the 40% year-over-year rise in cloud-native attacks reported by Mandiant's M-Trends report.

Overall blended average deal size across new and existing customers reached $620,000 in ACV terms, a 30% increase year-over-year. This outperforms the industry average of around $300,000-$400,000 for peers like Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Access deals or Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange, per recent Gartner Magic Quadrant data. The multi-year contract mix—now 82% of total bookings, with an average duration of 3.8 years—further bolsters our predictability, contributing to our $2.1 billion ARR run-rate, up 42% year-over-year.

Key trends fueling this growth include the bundling of our SASE suite with AI/ML-enhanced endpoint detection and response. In Q3, 45% of new logos included our SecureNet Fusion bundle, which integrates EDR, NGAV, and deception technology—delivering 4x faster mean-time-to-respond than legacy AV solutions. We've also seen a pivot to consumption-based pricing models, where customers pay based on protected endpoints or data volume, leading to larger initial commitments as they scale with us. This mirrors the industry's shift, with IDC forecasting SASE market growth to $15 billion by 2027 at 28% CAGR.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, accounting for 62% of Q3 bookings with an average new customer deal size of $520,000—buoyed by compliance drivers like SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules and the White House's Executive Order on quantum-resistant cryptography. EMEA followed at 25% of bookings, with deals averaging $410,000, propelled by GDPR enforcement and NIS2 Directive mandates; notable wins included a €50 million TCV expansion with a major German automotive OEM fortifying OT security against supply chain risks like those seen in SolarWinds.

APAC contributed 13% of bookings but with 42% year-over-year deal size expansion to $380,000 average for new customers. This is tied to Australia's Essential Eight maturity model updates and Singapore's Cybersecurity Act, where we're partnering with hyperscalers like Alibaba Cloud to embed our platform natively. Japan and India saw particularly strong traction, with deals 30% above regional average due to rising state-sponsored phishing campaigns.

Strategically, we're doubling down on technical initiatives like our GenAI Threat Hunter, which automates 75% of SOC triage workflows, enabling customers to justify larger expansions. We've also launched co-sell motions with Microsoft via the Azure Marketplace, capturing 20% of Q3 pipeline from joint pursuits. Looking ahead, we expect Q4 new customer average deal size to trend toward $480,000-$500,000, with existing expansions at $800,000 TCV, supported by our $1.2 billion RPO visibility. This deal size momentum underscores our competitive moat in a market where CISOs are prioritizing platform consolidation over point solutions—reducing vendor sprawl from 50+ to under 10, per ESG research. We're well-positioned to sustain 30%+ growth as cybersecurity spend hits 15% of IT budgets globally.

Before diving deeper into our outlook, I want to address a key factor influencing our reported results: the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations on revenue. As a global leader in next-generation cybersecurity platforms, with over 45% of our total revenue derived from international markets, we remain exposed to currency volatility—but our constant currency metrics underscore the underlying strength of our business.

For the quarter, we reported total revenue of $785 million, up 28% year-over-year as reported, and a robust 32% in constant currency terms. Annual Recurring Revenue reached $4.7 billion, growing 35% year-over-year on a constant currency basis, driven by strong adoption of our flagship SecureX Platform and AI-powered threat detection modules like QuantumShield and ZeroTrust Edge. However, foreign exchange headwinds shaved approximately $38 million, or 3%, off our top-line growth. This marks the third consecutive quarter of USD strength impacting our results, with the U.S. dollar appreciating 8% against a basket of our key trading currencies since Q3 FY2023.

Breaking it down regionally: EMEA, 38% of total revenue, contributed $486 million, up 25% year-over-year as reported but 31% in constant currency. The euro depreciated 6% against the USD quarter-over-quarter, creating a $22 million headwind—equivalent to 220 basis points of growth suppression. Despite this, EMEA remains our fastest-growing region, fueled by escalating ransomware campaigns targeting critical infrastructure. Our partnerships with hyperscalers like AWS and Azure have accelerated SecureX deployments in the DACH region, where we've seen 45% year-over-year ARR growth amid stringent GDPR compliance demands.

APAC, 22% of total revenue, totaled $282 million, reflecting 22% year-over-year growth as reported and 29% constant currency. The Japanese yen weakened 12% year-over-year, and the Australian dollar fell 4%, resulting in a $10 million FX drag. China-exposed revenue, now just 5% of APAC due to our deliberate pivot post-regulatory scrutiny, faced additional pressure from the offshore RMB's 7% decline. Positively, demand for our Cloud Native Application Protection Platform surged 40% in India and Southeast Asia, offsetting FX amid rising state-sponsored APT threats.

LATAM, 12% of total revenue, delivered $154 million, up 18% year-over-year reported and 26% constant currency. Volatility in the Brazilian real down 9% year-over-year and Mexican peso down 5% imposed a $6 million headwind. Our strategic focus on Mexico's nearshoring boom—protecting manufacturing supply chains from phishing and insider threats—drove 55% ARR expansion.

To mitigate these impacts, we've layered in several strategies aligning with our high-margin, subscription-heavy model: We've hedged 75% of our forecasted 12-month FX exposure as of quarter-end, primarily through forward contracts on euro, yen, and real exposures. This covered $850 million in projected international ARR, limiting our net FX sensitivity to under 1.5% of total revenue for FY2024. Our treasury team dynamically adjusts hedges based on Bloomberg FX volatility indices, targeting a 60-80% hedge ratio.

Additionally, 92% of our international deals are now denominated in local currencies, up from 82% last year. This shields us from translational FX swings. We've also implemented AI-driven dynamic pricing algorithms in our CPQ system, adjusting for local inflation and threat intensity—boosting win rates by 12% in volatile markets. Our Remaining Performance Obligations grew 42% year-over-year to $9.2 billion, with 55% from international customers. We're accelerating U.S. and stable-currency expansions, like our new Singapore hub serving APAC, while investing in edge computing integrations for low-latency threat hunting. This diversification reduced our net FX exposure by 15% year-over-year.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 FX headwinds of $25-30 million, assuming current spot rates hold, but our constant currency revenue guidance remains strong, implying 30%+ growth. Rising global cyber threats—per our Q3 Threat Report showing a 65% uptick in zero-day exploits—should continue driving multi-year contracts, insulating us from short-term FX noise.

I'll now turn to our full-year fiscal 2024 outlook, which reflects the robust demand environment we're seeing across the cybersecurity landscape. As you know, the global cybersecurity market is projected by Gartner to grow at a 13.8% CAGR through 2028, driven by escalating threats like ransomware-as-a-service—think LockBit and BlackCat variants—and the proliferation of generative AI vulnerabilities, as highlighted in our recent Q3 Threat Landscape Report. We've positioned SecureNet Technologies at the forefront of this with our AI-native XDR platform, SecureXDR 5.0, which integrates endpoint detection and response, network security, and cloud workload protection into a unified agentless architecture.

For the full year, we're guiding to revenue of $3.05 billion to $3.15 billion, representing approximately 22% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. This compares favorably to our fiscal 2023 results of $2.52 billion and outperforms the consensus analyst estimate of $3.02 billion.

Subscription and SaaS revenue, which now comprises 82% of our total ARR—up from 78% last year—will be the primary growth engine. We expect this segment to deliver $2.55 billion to $2.65 billion, or 25% growth. Key tailwinds include a net retention rate of 118% in Q3, fueled by expanding multi-product adoption. Customers deploying our SecureXDR platform alongside our Cloud Native Application Protection Platform are upsellling at a 35% attach rate. We've also seen strong momentum in our SecureIdentity solution, our identity threat detection and response offering, with deeper behavioral analytics powered by our proprietary ML models trained on 10 trillion daily signals.

Product revenue, primarily from our next-gen firewalls and secure access service edge appliances, is forecasted at $350 million to $370 million, flat to up 5% as we strategically shift toward cloud-delivered models. Our SASE bundle, SecureEdge, has gained traction post our integration with Microsoft Azure Virtual WAN, capturing share in the hybrid work era.

Professional services and other revenue will contribute $150 million to $170 million, up 10%, driven by managed detection and response contracts tied to our analyst workflows.

Geographically, the Americas remain our bedrock at ~52% of revenue, with expected growth of 20% amid U.S. federal mandates like CISA's zero-trust directives and the Biden administration's 2024 Executive Order on quantum-resistant cryptography. EMEA, at 28% of mix, accelerates to 28% growth, propelled by NIS2 Directive compliance and GDPR fines exceeding €2.7 billion last year alone—our partnerships with Deutsche Telekom and Orange Business Services are yielding 40% year-over-year ACV expansion here. APAC, now 20% of revenue, is our fastest-growing region at 32% growth, thanks to Australia's Essential Eight framework updates and Singapore's Cybersecurity Act. We've doubled down with a new Tokyo data center and localized offerings for China's MLPS 2.0 regulations, offsetting any U.S.-China tensions via our China-Compliant Cloud tier.

On profitability, we're committed to operating leverage as we scale. Non-GAAP gross margins are guided to 82% to 83%, expanding 150 basis points from fiscal 2023's 80.5%, primarily from a higher mix of high-margin SaaS at 86% margins and efficiencies in our autonomous SOC operations, which reduced mean-time-to-detect to under 5 minutes via GenAI triage.

Operating expenses as a percentage of revenue will decline to 54% to 55%, down from 58% last year, yielding non-GAAP operating margins of 27% to 28%—a 300 basis points expansion. This includes R&D investments at 14% of revenue, focused on post-quantum cryptography readiness with NIST-approved Kyber and Dilithium algorithms integrated into SecureXDR and OT/IoT security for critical infrastructure, addressing vulnerabilities exposed in the 2024 Change Healthcare ransomware incident.

Adjusted EBITDA is expected at $825 million to $875 million, or 27% margins at the midpoint, with free cash flow conversion exceeding 110%. Diluted non-GAAP EPS guidance is $4.65 to $4.85, based on ~195 million fully diluted shares, assuming a 21% effective tax rate. GAAP net income will benefit from our $500 million share repurchase authorization, with $200 million deployed year-to-date at an average of $145 per share.

This outlook embeds several technical initiatives. First, the GA launch of SecureXDR 5.0 in Q4, featuring agentless cloud detection with 99.9% accuracy against zero-day exploits, positions us as a leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for XDR—where we debuted as a Visionary last year, challenging CrowdStrike's Falcon and Microsoft Defender XDR. Second, our $450 million acquisition of ThreatForge bolsters supply chain risk management, critical post-SolarWinds and MOVEit breaches. Third, hyperscaler integrations—AWS Bedrock for AI security copilot, Google Chronicle for SIEM fusion—drive 25% of new logos.

Macro trends support this: IDC forecasts endpoint security spend up 16% to $12.5 billion in 2024, while SASE hits $4.4 billion per Forrester. However, risks include elongated sales cycles in discretionary IT budgets currently at 90 days versus 75 historical, forex headwinds impacting 25% international revenue, and competitive intensity from Fortinet's FortiGate consolidations.

We're confident in delivering the upper half of this guidance, underpinned by a $4.2 billion backlog—up 30% year-over-year—and pipeline visibility at 3.5x ARR targets.

Next, Taylor Kim will provide more technical details.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. We continue to innovate and push the boundaries of what's possible in cybersecurity. Our team is focused on developing cutting-edge solutions that address the evolving threat landscape. We are investing heavily in research and development to stay ahead of the curve and deliver unparalleled value to our customers. Key areas of focus include advancements in average deal sizes through platform expansions like our SecureXDR integrations, which have driven larger multi-product deployments.

Morgan Patel: Thank you. Cybersecurity is paramount, and we are taking proactive measures to protect our customers and ourselves. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance, including rigorous adherence to global regulations like NIS2, GDPR, and FedRAMP, while enhancing our hedging and localization strategies to counter currency risks in international operations.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session. At this time, to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. First question comes from Sarah Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Sarah Chen: Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter. Can you elaborate on the full-year guidance and how you're thinking about profitability margins amid R&D investments?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Sarah. As Jordan detailed, our full-year revenue guide of $3.05 to $3.15 billion reflects 22% growth at the midpoint, with non-GAAP operating margins expanding to 27-28%. We're balancing aggressive R&D in post-quantum crypto and GenAI defenses with operating leverage from our SaaS mix, confident in the upper half given our backlog and pipeline.

Operator: Next question comes from David Patel with Goldman Sachs.

David Patel: Great, thanks. On new customer acquisition and deal sizes—how sustainable is the 28% YoY new logo growth and the $450K average for new customers?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, David. The 520 new customers and $450K new ACV reflect our land-and-expand strength, driven by Sentinel AI launches and hyperscaler partnerships. With pipeline up 40% and Q4 guide of 550-600 adds, plus expansions pushing NRR to 128%, this momentum is durable in a consolidating market.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Torres with JPMorgan.

Lisa Torres: Thank you. Taylor, could you speak more to the technical innovations addressing the threat landscape, like in ransomware and supply chain?

Taylor Kim: Absolutely, Lisa. Our SecureXDR 5.0 blocks LockBit variants with 99.9% zero-day accuracy via agentless architecture, and ThreatForge acquisition fortifies supply chain SCRM. GenAI Shield detects deepfakes at 98.7% TPR, keeping us ahead of the 62% surge in high-severity incidents.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Reynolds with Barclays.

Mike Reynolds: Thanks. Jordan, with FX headwinds at $38 million this quarter, how are you mitigating ongoing currency impacts?

Alex Rivera: Good question, Mike. Jordan covered our 75% hedging on $850M exposure and 92% local currency contracts, reducing sensitivity to 1.5%. Constant currency growth was 32%, and Q4 headwinds of $25-30M are more than offset by threat-driven demand.

Alex Rivera: Thank you all for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. Thank you to our dedicated employees, loyal customers, and valued partners.

Casey Wong: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
